newsitem.title: USA: Texaco chief says minority plan in works.
newsitem.headline: Texaco chief says minority plan in works.

text.p: Texaco Inc's Chief Executive Peter Bijur said on Wednesday the company will release a plan to develop more minority programs but warned he would not be pressured by civil rights groups on the timetable for the report.
"We're going to take the appropriate action," Bijur said after the company's annual meeting with security analysts at its headquarters. "But I won't do it with a gun to my head," he added.
Texaco settled a civil suit with 1,400 black employees in mid-November for $115 million. The company's black employees also received salary hikes.

Civil rights leaders including the Rev. Jesse Jackson and Kweisi Mfume of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People have called for a sustained boycott against Texaco because they were disappointed with progress on the company's plan.
Mfume has said he expects to see Texaco's plan by December 13, though he said the company appeared to have done little preparation.
Bijur said minority employment inside Texaco had increased in recent years while the total number of employees had declined. But he would not say the problem had been eradicated.
"I would not be presumptuous enough to say we'd be a model for anybody," he said.
"I just want to put this behind us," he added.
